question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no 4.
solution:
The correct answer is '**without**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The context of the sentence suggests that you can act freely ("roll him triumphantly in the dust") without worrying about repercussions ("fear of a counterstroke").
 
• "Without" best conveys the idea of not having to fear any counter-attacks or responses.
 
• "**Without**" aligns well with the intended meaning, indicating an absence of fear.
 
• Other options ("**in**", "**for**", "**with**") do not convey this absence of fear and are grammatically incorrect in the context.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

Complete Passage: *There is a pleasant__ sense of freedom about being alone in a carriage that is jolting noisily through the night. It is liberty unrestrained in a very **__agreeable__ form. You can do anything you like. You can talk to **__yourself__ as loud as you please and no one will hear you. You can have that argument out with Jones and roll him triumphantly in the dust **__without__** fear of a counterstroke. You can stand on your head and no one will see you. You can sing or dance a two-step or practise a golf stroke, (5) ______ play marbles on the floor without let or hindrance.* 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 
• **In**: Incorrect as it does not convey the idea of absence of fear in the context.
 
• **For**: Incorrect as it changes the intended meaning and is grammatically improper.
 
• **With**: Incorrect as it implies having the fear, which is the opposite of what is meant.
